summary: Set insertion with deduplication: linearly scans the integer set stored as a linked list rooted at this+0x18. If the input value a2 is already present, returns 1 (duplicate). Otherwise allocates a 4-byte cell, stores a2, appends a node via LinkedListNodeAppend_6000 with flag 1, and returns 0.

operations.description: Initialize result to 1, the already-present marker returned when the set already contains the value.
Read the list head from this+0x18; if it is null the set is empty and control jumps to the insertion path.
Linear traversal of the linked list starting at the head, following each node's next pointer until a null next pointer ends the scan.
Compare each node's stored value (first dword of the node reached through the pointer at this+0x1C) against a2; a match exits the scan to return the duplicate marker.
Allocate a 4-byte cell for the integer value via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper.
Store the input value a2 into the allocated cell.
Append the new node to the list via LinkedListNodeAppend_6000 with flag argument 1; on allocation failure the same append is attempted with a null node.
Return 0 for a new insertion, or 1 when the value was already present.

unresolved: Purpose of the list-related field at this+0x20 is not expressed in the raw body.
Node bookkeeping (head/tail/count maintenance) is owned by LinkedListNodeAppend_6000 and is not reconstructed here.
